SearchAliases: know hot and cold for oneself
Senses.Explanation: Knowing hot and cold for oneself is the recurrent predicate of the drinking-water comparison: the person concerned, not another reporter, knows the temperature. Literally, one knows cold and warmth for oneself, usually in the comparison “like a person drinking water, knowing hot and cold for himself” . Huiming uses it after Huineng's instruction to report that he now has an entry; Huangbo joins it to conduct in each movement, dwelling, and instant; and other teachers pair it with looking for oneself rather than seeking from another. The phrase also becomes an object of interrogation: Longmen Foyan grants that hot and cold can be known, then asks what the one who knows for himself is. Daodu pairs “knowing hot and cold for oneself” with “handling slow and urgent matters for oneself” and says the matter cannot be spoken out even when both parties exert themselves. The Chan bend is this sensory commonplace's use as a first-person report, an answer about the Way, and a question about the knower; the texts preserve the water comparison and these recorded deployments.

Senses.Explanation: Its recorded neighbors make the image concrete: “the cold furnace has no smoke; a bean pops in cold ashes” (寒爐煙絕，冷灰豆爆); a public question asks, “leaving aside a withered tree flowering, what about when a bean pops in cold ashes?” and receives “a thunderclap on level ground” (平地一聲雷). Other addresses follow the phrase with impossible growth—stone bamboo shoots sprout, flame comes from an icy river, an iron tree flowers, and a wooden man claps—or simply with “suddenly, one sound” (驀地一聲). The corpus also speaks of “a person in whom a bean has popped in cold ashes” (冷灰豆爆底人), making the image an appraisal in an interview. Zen bends a domestic image of an unlikely pop from spent ash into a stock address and interview phrase, repeatedly paired with sound and impossible renewal. Those pairings are the texts’ own; this entry assigns no hidden event to the image.

SearchAliases: Deshan goes down with his bowl
Senses.Explanation: The case title “Deshan Carries His Bowl” names the complete Deshan–Xuefeng–Yantou encounter, not merely the initial movement with a meal bowl. The case records Deshan going down with his bowl before bell or drum; Xuefeng asks where he is going, Deshan returns to his quarters, Xuefeng reports this to Yantou, and Yantou says Deshan has not understood the last phrase. Deshan summons Yantou, who privately states his meaning; the next day's ascent of the seat differs from usual, and Yantou says Deshan will live only three more years. The corpus turns this named encounter into a case heading, verse topic, question asked at the teaching seat, assigned object of inquiry, and point of later prose comment. Recorded replies to 'what is its meaning?' include 'no meaning' followed by 'if he wanted to go, he went; if he wanted to sit, he sat,' and, elsewhere, 'buying dear and selling cheap.'

Senses.Explanation: Cutting off the arm is the bodily action attributed to Huike and raised repeatedly as a named ancestral case. In the Chan record it overwhelmingly names the founding episode in which Shenguang, later named Huike, stands in the snow before Bodhidharma, cuts off his left arm, and places it before him. The lamp account has Bodhidharma say, 'you have now cut off your arm before me; your seeking may be accepted,' and then rename him Huike. Later records compress the episode into paired formulas—'standing in the snow and cutting off the arm,' 'cutting off the arm and pacifying the mind,' or 'face the wall for nine years / cut off the arm and pacify the mind'—and repeatedly reopen it as a public question. Huike asks, 'what did the cutting off of the arm accomplish?' and strikes the staff before leaving the seat. Another is asked why one cuts off an arm to seek the Way if this house style is inherent in everyone; he replies, 'there are many mistaken understandings.' Still another says, 'why cut off an arm and seek elsewhere?' The Chan-specific bend is that Huike's bodily act becomes compact lineage and interview language, quoted, challenged, and criticized across later records. These later uses do not authorize this entry to declare the act a required sacrifice or explain its intention beyond what the accounts say.

The records use this transitive appraisal for seeing through a saying, case, person, condition, or position before or after it is presented. Literally, 'look through' or 'look and break through.' The compound occurs 509 times in 154 allowed texts. It is used transitively of a saying, case, person, condition, or distinction; in passive clauses someone or something is 'seen through.' Hongzhi asks, 'What is the eye with which you can see through it?'. Comments on earlier cases say that someone saw through Lingyun and Mahakasyapa, that Tianning saw through Dahui, or that an interlocutor should see through an action before it occurs. The passive form appears in a warning about being seen through by someone at a later time (他時異日被人覷破). The fuller form 'be able to see through' occurs 40 times in 25 texts, while the emphatic 'with one look, see through' (一覷覷破) occurs 19 times in 17. The texts do not supply a separate technical definition beyond these observable objects, contrasts, questions, and active/passive constructions.
Senses.Note: The two hits for 'one who sees through this' use the final graph as the pronoun 'this,' not as a definition formula. They were therefore not treated as self-definitions. The corpus range is grammatical rather than polysemous: the same verb occurs with people, words, cases, and named distinctions as its object.

Senses.Explanation: To buy a hat by measuring the head is to choose the hat by first taking the wearer’s measure. Tiantong Jue pairs the phrase with deciding whether someone is son or thief and removing bones before eating fish. Xutang says simply, “here I buy a hat by measuring the head,” while the Collected Essentials calls an exact fit difficult. These clauses establish measured fitting and discriminating selection; they do not by themselves define it as conceptual calculation.
